purpose: OsteotomyCuts is a scripted 3D Slicer module (Planning category) for virtual osteotomy planning in orthognathic and craniofacial surgery: the user draws cut lines on a bone model and the bone is split into closed segments, with distance checks to nerve canals and tooth roots. It is aimed at surgeons and researchers using Slicer on de-identified or research models.
summary: I found no malicious or concealed behaviour and no data egress. The only network-related code is a local read-only `git rev-parse` call, and there are no URL fetches, pip installs, or pickle/eval use in the module. Test-code `os.remove` calls only delete the test's own temp scene. Packaging is simple (no build dependencies, EXTENSION_DEPENDS "NA" consistent with the entry). The GPL-3.0 LICENSE is present in full. Main concerns are process: the catalog tracks `main` while the author's notes say the v1.0.0 release is not yet authorised, and the CLA is marked as an unreviewed draft. I could not inspect the 408 KB module fully, the .ui files, or the remote commit.

safety.rationale: Searched OsteotomyCuts.py for network, subprocess, pip, eval/exec, pickle, os.system, sys.path and environ use. Only a local `git rev-parse` (lines 4332-4334) and temp-file removals in test code (lines 5916-5923) were found; no telemetry or URL fetches (only doc links and a QSettings disclaimer flag at lines 898/917).

environment.rationale: No pip_install, no sys.path edits, no global logging or warnings changes were found in the search. Heavy imports (scipy) are inside functions with guards (lines 229, 2373-2375, 2529, 2613). Only numpy/qt/vtk are imported at module level, which Slicer provides.

packaging.rationale: CMakeLists.txt uses slicerMacroBuildScriptedModule with listed scripts and resources, and EXTENSION_DEPENDS "NA" matches the empty build_dependencies in the entry. I did not confirm that Resources/Icons/OsteotomyCuts.png exists (the listing shows only '1 files') or that the Testing/Python run_*.py scripts are present. The catalog entry tracks the branch 'main' rather than a pinned revision.

license.rationale: LICENSE is the full GPL-3.0 text (35 KB), and CMake and source headers declare GPL-3.0-or-later. No bundled third-party code was seen. The README's commercial dual-licence offer does not restrict GPL distribution.

soundness.rationale: I read only the git helper, a test round-trip, and the module header. The module is large and was not reviewed in full, so I make no claim about the cutting algorithm. The module-level `from slicer.ScriptedLoadableModule import *` is a style issue.

utility.rationale: There is a README with quick start and limitations, a DISCLAIMER, COMPATIBILITY and RELEASE_NOTES, and a headless test suite. The CMake test registration for Testing/Python is commented out (OsteotomyCuts/Testing/Python/CMakeLists.txt line 6), and the CLA is labelled a draft. Tier 1 is declared.

findings.title: Catalog entry tracks branch 'main' while the author's notes describe an unreleased pre-release on another branch
findings.evidence:
- v1.0.0 pre-release (branch `release`, from 3a7458d = Phase 2, no Phase 3):
  Parts 0-10 of the user's to-do list, done in order, stopping after each
  for testing in Slicer. Phase 3 work continues on `master` and is merged
  after the release (Part 10). Nothing is pushed publicly, tagged or put
findings.explanation: The entry sets scm_revision to "main", so whatever is on main at install time is what users get, and the reviewed commit 30e57a6 cannot be pinned from the entry. CLAUDE.md says the v1.0.0 release is on branch `release` and that nothing is to be published or put into a pull request until the author types GO RELEASE. Whether main currently holds the approved release is unclear, so the code users receive may not match what was reviewed or released.
findings.suggestion: Ask the author to confirm which commit is the intended release, and pin scm_revision to that commit or a tag in the catalog entry.

findings.title: CLA is marked as an unreviewed draft
findings.evidence: > **Draft — to be reviewed by a legal professional.**
findings.explanation: CLA.md, which contributors are asked to sign, says it has not been reviewed by a lawyer. Contributors may be unsure what they are granting, and the project's dual-licence model depends on this text. This does not affect distribution under GPL-3.0, which is covered by the full LICENSE file.
findings.suggestion: Have the CLA reviewed before the dual-licence offer is relied on, or remove the draft banner once it is approved.

findings.title: Test registration commented out in Testing/Python
findings.explanation: OsteotomyCuts/Testing/Python/CMakeLists.txt only has the test line commented out, so no module-specific ctest is registered. The main module CMakeLists still runs slicer_add_python_unittest on OsteotomyCuts.py when BUILD_TESTING is set, so the impact is limited.
findings.suggestion: Remove the dead line or register the headless test runner as a ctest.

findings.title: Local git helper runs a subprocess once per session
findings.evidence:
result = subprocess.run(["git", "rev-parse", "--short", "HEAD"], cwd=os.path.dirname(__file__),
                                        capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=5,
findings.explanation: moduleGitHash runs `git rev-parse` in the module's folder with a 5 s timeout to record provenance. It is read-only and local, and it falls back to 'unknown' on error. It is noted for transparency only.
findings.suggestion: No change required. Optionally drop the subprocess call from the shipped module.

not_checked: Most of the 7,396-line OsteotomyCuts.py was not read (only targeted searches and about 100 lines); the cutting algorithm, GUI code and tests were not reviewed in full.
The Resources/UI/*.ui files and Resources/Icons/OsteotomyCuts.png were not inspected, so their existence and content were not verified.
The remote repository at scm_url and revision 30e57a6 were not accessed; the main branch tip was not compared with the reviewed commit.
Test scripts referenced in the docs (run_headless_tests.py etc.) were not opened; no tests were run and no build was attempted.
Clinical validity of distance checks and the cut algorithm were not assessed; no model or patient data was read.
